page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.large is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T24 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It includes 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing in the top 25% at 3059.78. However, multi-core scaling is limited due to the 2-vCPU configuration, resulting in a weak multi-core CPU performance rating in stress-ng (3062.79) and Geekbench (2433.0). Memory performance is mixed; while large-block write bandwidth is average at 27.53 GB/sec, cached small-block read bandwidth is poor at 150.55 GB/sec. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks perform at average levels, but database operations and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, with web serving throughput measured at 2.79 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.c8a.large offers a cost-efficient entry point for compute-focused workloads that require dedicated CPU execution but have low memory footprints. The lack of local storage and modest network bandwidth make it less suitable for high-throughput database operations or heavy web serving. It is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded compute tasks, basic text processing, software compilation, and general-purpose utility workloads that do not demand extensive memory or high multi-threaded concurrency.
